title: Human hippocampal ripples align new experiences with a grid-like schema
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Whole-paper targets are learning/rest ripple effects, grid-like modulation and its relationships to behavior, and ripple-aligned cortical HFB associations. Review also considered the original ripple detector and participant inference task. No originally evaluated computational prediction/recovery accuracy target was found; this is not a restriction imposed by the legacy registration.

Source-paper comparison for No eligible original computational-performance metric recovered from the whole paper: Source outputs include mixed-model coefficients, Learn-R, robust partial correlations and grid beta1/orientation estimates. Maximizing these is not algorithm improvement. Human feature/inference accuracy is an observed participant outcome, while the paper provides neither an author machine-solver score under matched exposure nor a ground-truth detector/recovery benchmark.
success_criteria: No active same-task computational paper win is admitted on the basis of this whole-paper review; the legacy reconstruction does not determine eligibility.
Do not reward larger ripple slopes, correlations, grid modulation, smaller p-values or better agreement with supplied coefficients as performance improvement.
Do not convert the odd/even grid coefficient analysis into an unreported predictive-loss or orientation-recovery benchmark.
Do not replace the original human participants with a machine solver and compare its score to their behavioral accuracy as the same neural-data task.

Any subsequently recovered computational endpoint actually evaluated in this same source paper may reopen eligibility; an invented held-patient decoder or the paper's proposed future replay analysis is an extension.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.

blocking_issues: Whole-paper computational analyses assess biological effects, associations and modulation, without an eligible ordered original algorithm-performance endpoint.
The odd/even grid procedure refits modulation on its test half and reports beta1; no predictive-loss or known-orientation recovery baseline is supplied.
The reported human behavioral accuracy cannot become a machine-solver baseline without changing the scientific population and intervention.
The threshold ripple detector is not evaluated against ground-truth event labels, and content-specific replay decoding is discussed as future work; neither provides an original task baseline.
